evidence: src/infrastructure/server.ts: createServer(repository: Repository) creates one `new TaskService(repository)`, and every route handler uses it.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: route handlers call only taskService methods (createProject, createUser, addTask, assignTask, markTaskDone, listTasks). There is no direct repository access.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: the per-route checks (`if (!id || !name)`, `if (!assigneeId)`) only check the request shape and leave domain rules to TaskService.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: all errors go through `next(error)` to a single app.use error handler, so error mapping lives in one place.
Minor: `status: status as any` in the GET /projects/:projectId/tasks handler weakens type safety. It is not a cohesion or abstraction bypass.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module has one file, src/infrastructure/server.ts, and it does one job: it is the HTTP adapter. createServer builds an Express app, wires a single TaskService instance over the injected Repository, and sends every route through that service (createProject, createUser, addTask, assignTask, markTaskDone, listTasks). No route touches the repository or domain entities directly, so the application abstraction is used consistently. The presence checks in each route (for example `if (!id || !name)` on /projects and /users) only validate request shape. They are not domain invariants, and the business rules stay in TaskService. Errors from every route go to one central error-handling middleware. Some things could be improved, but none of them break this rule: `status as any` sidesteps typing when building the listTasks filter, and the error handler turns every error into a 400. Neither one splits the file's concern, duplicates a domain rule, or bypasses the module's abstractions.
